title: Skipped disclosure and risky statements
description: Sales call. The agent never states the recording disclosure, claims there is no waiting period for diabetes, promises claim approval, and quotes a price and pushes the payment link without disclosing waiting periods.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hello, this is Rahul from Nivaran Health. Am I speaking with Mrs. Kavita Sharma?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You had asked about a family health plan. Who would you like to cover?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Me, my husband and our daughter. My husband has diabetes.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No problem at all. With our Family Floater everything is covered from day one, there is no waiting period for diabetes.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Really? I thought there was always a waiting period for diabetes.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Don't worry madam, your claim will definitely be approved, it is a hundred percent guaranteed.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. What would it cost for ten lakh cover?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: For ten lakh, the premium is around seventeen thousand eight hundred rupees a year. Shall I send you the payment link now?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Let me think about it. Is the payment link safe?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Yes, it is our official link. You can pay by card or UPI.
